caption: The drawing consists of a main central object and two smaller inset diagrams at the lower left and right. The central object is an elongated, intricate wall plaque or mount depicted in shades of gray pencil on an off-white or beige paper background. It has a symmetric, curving outline with a bulbous top and bottom and a pinched middle, with a circular element near the top and a larger oval or round shape in the vertical center. Emerging from the lower portion of the larger central circle is a structured, vertical element resembling a candle or mechanical part, with a gear-like ring and linear grooves extending downward, ending in a more squared-off segment. In the lower left margin, there is a small rectangular inset showing a side profile of a wavy vertical rod with a horizontal platform or bracket extending from it. In the lower right margin, another rectangular inset illustrates a front view of the same or similar rod with a circular detail at the bottom and includes marked scales below labeled "SCALE OF DETAILS." The artist's name, "FRANCIS LAW DURAND," is inscribed at the bottom right. The overall composition is contained within a double-rectangular border, and detailed shading provides dimensionality to the objects.
title: Wall Sconce
cluster: #16 — Lighting Devices: Lamps, Lanterns, and Candleholders
